sections.h2: Ways to sell a New Brunswick house fast
sections.html:
A New Brunswick owner has three realistic paths. An agent listing reaches the most buyers, a private sale saves the commission, and a direct as-is purchase trades some price for speed. Whichever you pick, the deed is recorded at the Middlesex County Clerk's office on Bayard Street, inside the city.

This is a renter city. The owner-occupied rate is just 21.4% for 2020 to 2024, across 15,676 households of about 3.13 people each, and the population estimate for July 2025 is 57,133. A sale here often involves a house with tenants or a landlord seller, so the rental rules below matter as much as the repair list. The middle owner-occupied value is $353,800.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure, though showings, repairs and a lender's timetable come with it.
  • Private sale: no commission, but you still need an attorney, a deed and the municipal paperwork.
  • As-is purchase: often no lender and a closing date you set, with the house taken in its current state. Repairs and showings drop away.

Hospital staff, students and commuters make up much of the demand. Johnson & Johnson keeps its global headquarters here beside several medical teaching and research institutions, Rutgers has three campuses inside city limits, and Robert Wood Johnson Medical School spans New Brunswick and Piscataway.

Commuting shapes the buyer pool too. Residents spend 23.3 minutes getting to work on average, and the city sits on the Northeast Corridor rail line between New York and Trenton. Route 18, U.S. 1 and Route 27 cross the city.

  • Hospital and university staff looking for a short commute.
  • Landlords weighing a rental house against the city's rent control rules.
  • Households who want rail access to Penn Station.

When you describe your house to a buyer, name the neighborhood it sits in: the Fifth Ward, Feaster Park, Lincoln Park, Raritan Gardens or Edgebrook-Westons Mills. It paints a clearer picture than the street address alone.

Start with the alarm check. New Brunswick's Division of Fire Safety inspects smoke detectors and carbon monoxide alarms in one and two family houses being sold or leased, and it offers an online form for booking the visit. Schedule it early so a dead battery does not push the closing back.

The Construction Department, at 25 Kirkpatrick Street, also issues a Certificate of Continuing Occupancy when the city calls for one. Phone 732-745-5075 and ask whether your sale needs it. The answer depends on the property and its permit history.

If tenants live in the house, read the Rent Control Ordinance before you list. Most rental units in the city are regulated, and each regulated unit must register by April 1 every year. Owners of unregistered units face summonses and fines, so confirm your registration status with the Rent Control office first.

Winters bring snow, so clear the gutters and check the roof before the first showing.

sections.h2: Rent control and your rental's price
sections.html:
Rent control caps what a landlord can collect. Rents may rise only by the yearly allowance unless the unit has an approved vacancy decontrol or is exempt, so the rent roll you show is the figure a buyer will work from.

For 2027 the registration fee is $55 per unit, doubled if the form comes in after April 30. A vacancy adjustment costs $60 a unit and a market vacancy decontrol $175. The office answers questions at 732-745-5050 or rentcontrol@cityofnewbrunswick.org, and it can explain the changes that began January 1, 2026.

Filing the deed triggers the state realty transfer fee, and the seller pays it. The fee rises in bands with the price, and above $350,000 a second schedule begins that reaches $4.80 for each $500 of price in the $200,000 to $550,000 band. With the middle local value at $353,800, many sales land in that higher schedule. The settlement statement from your closing attorney shows the exact fee.

Sellers who live out of state have an extra task at the closing table. At least two percent of the deed price is paid ahead toward New Jersey income tax unless a GIT/REP-3 assurance fits. New Jersey residents sign that same form instead, and whoever runs the closing normally fills out the right one.

sections.h2: Recording the deed with the county
sections.html:
Filings go to the Middlesex County Clerk's registry on the fourth floor of the County Administration Building, 75 Bayard Street. The office is open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:10, though the last arrivals are taken at 4 pm. The main line is 732-745-3002, and walk-ins are welcome, with appointments served first.

  • Documents must be readable English with original signatures, printed names and a proper acknowledgment.
  • A deed carries the drafter's name after the words Prepared by, plus tax block, lot and the price.
  • A return address is required.
  • Paper filings need a cover sheet or the county adds a $20 indexing charge.

Attorneys and title companies may instead send documents any hour of the day through the county's e-recording portal. Owners worried about fraud on an empty house can sign up for the clerk's email alerts, which announce any document recorded against their block and lot.

sections.h2: How a quick sale usually runs here
sections.html:
Order matters, because several offices have to be dealt with before a closing date can be firm. Book the Division of Fire Safety alarm check first, since it is online and fast. Call the Construction Department about the Certificate of Continuing Occupancy next. If the house has tenants, pull together the leases, the rent history and your Rent Control registration so a buyer can see what the units bring in.

Then sort out the deed. Your attorney drafts it with the tax block, lot and price, you sign it with the proper acknowledgment, and the county records it after closing. If you live out of state, the GIT/REP form is signed at the same table. A buyer paying cash and taking the house as it stands skips the lender's appraisal and repair demands, which is where many conventional closings slip. The paperwork above still applies either way.

faqs.q: Can a New Brunswick house be sold while tenants are still in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale does not end a tenancy. Keep your rent control registration current and have each lease and the rent history on hand, because regulated units register by April 1 every year and unregistered ones risk fines.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required before selling a small home in New Brunswick?
faqs.a: At minimum a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm check through the Division of Fire Safety for one and two family houses. Call the Construction Department at 732-745-5075 to learn whether a Certificate of Continuing Occupancy is also needed.

faqs.q: Which office files the deed after a New Brunswick sale?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Clerk's registry, in the County Administration Building on Bayard Street. Your closing attorney or title company usually submits it, either on paper or electronically.

faqs.q: I own the house but live in another state. What changes?
faqs.a: You complete a GIT/REP form at the closing table. A nonresident seller prepays at least two percent of the deed price toward state income tax unless the GIT/REP-3 assurances apply, and can request a refund later if less is owed.

faqs.q: Which transfer fee schedule applies to a New Brunswick sale?
faqs.a: The lower schedule applies at $350,000 or less: $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, $3.35 per $500 up to $200,000, then $3.90 per $500 on the rest. One dollar over that figure moves the whole sale to the higher schedule.
